newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-Northern Italian club warns fans not to go south.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-Northern Italian club warns fans not to go south.

text.p: Northern soccer club Vicenza warned its fans against travelling south to Naples for a league match this weekend after violence at the Italian cup final between the two cities on Thursday night.
Vicenza won the two-leg final 3-1 on aggregate for the first trophy of their 95-year history after a second leg in Vicenza that turned into a north-south battle.
Around 30 people were hurt in clashes and police on Friday said the injured included a 25-year-old Vicenza fan who was stabbed in the leg outside the stadium.
Helmeted riot police baton-charged the Napoli end of the Romeo Menti stadium when fighting broke out after the final whistle, forcing many fans against fencing.
Most of the injured, none of them serious, were Napoli fans, hospital sources said.
The two clubs play each other again in the final match of the league season on Sunday, this time in Naples, with neither club having anything to play for beyond pride.
Vicenza football club said in a statement that they had received "numerous threatening phone calls from so-called Napoli fans towards the team and Vicenza fans leaving for Naples."
It warned fans of "the risks and concrete dangers that you face in travelling to the San Paolo stadium" and suggested that they avoid "this high-risk match"
Around 3,000 Napoli supporters had travelled north from Naples for Thursday's game, which carried strong racist overtones.
Banners and slogans supporting Northern separatists and the Northern League party, which is campaigning for a separate state in affluent northern Italy, were visible at the match.
One compared Naples unfavourably with the Albanian capital Tirana and another said "No to immigration".
Napoli supporters had hurled red flares and fireworks directly at Vicenza fans throughout the match.
Vicenza is in the northeast Veneto region, where the frustration with central government and high taxes that has fuelled separatist sentiment runs high.
The League, and smaller separatist groups, have sought to depict southerners as lazy and criminal and complain that taxes on earnings in the north subsidise the less developed south.
